skill.name: opentargets-database
skill.description: Query the Open Targets Platform for target-disease associations, drug evidence, tractability, safety annotations, and drug repurposing signals.
skill.summary: Search and interpret Open Targets Platform data for therapeutic target discovery.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by documented Open Targets API access, Markdown code fences, inline identifiers, and biomedical terminology. I found no evidence of prompt injection, credential access, arbitrary command execution, malicious persistence, or data exfiltration beyond expected public API queries.

remediation.issue: The helper script sends user-provided search terms and identifiers to the public Open Targets API.
remediation.suggestion: Document this network behavior clearly for users and keep the destination restricted to the official Open Targets endpoint.

remediation.issue: The documentation includes many fenced Python examples that can trigger command-execution heuristics.
remediation.suggestion: Label examples as documentation and avoid shell-style snippets unless they are required.

content.user_title: Explore Open Targets Drug Discovery Data
content.value_statement: Drug discovery teams need reliable ways to connect genes, diseases, evidence, and known drugs. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Open Targets queries and evidence interpretation.
actual_capabilities: Search Open Targets entities by gene, disease, or drug name.
Retrieve target annotations, including tractability, safety, and genetic constraint data.
Summarize target-disease evidence from genetics, known drugs, pathways, expression, animal models, and literature.
Find known drugs for a disease with target, mechanism, phase, and status context.
Explain Open Targets identifiers, GraphQL endpoints, pagination, and common query patterns.
Support target prioritization workflows using association scores and evidence breakdowns.
limitations: The skill depends on the public Open Targets API and network availability.
Association scores are ranking metrics and do not predict clinical success.
Large systematic analyses should use downloads or BigQuery instead of repeated API calls.
Results require expert biological and clinical review before research decisions.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Targets For A Disease
use_cases.description: Identify top associated genes, inspect evidence types, and compare tractability and safety signals.

use_cases.title: Validate A Candidate Gene
use_cases.description: Review target annotations, disease associations, known drugs, and safety liabilities for a nominated gene.

use_cases.title: Map Repurposing Opportunities
use_cases.description: Find drugs linked to a disease and compare mechanisms, targets, clinical phases, and related indications.

prompt_templates.title: Search Basic Entity IDs
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup for identifiers before deeper analysis.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Open Targets for the gene BRCA1 and the disease Alzheimer disease. Return the best matching identifiers and explain why each match is likely correct.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize A Target Profile
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Open Targets to summarize BRAF target annotations. Include tractability, safety concerns, genetic constraint, and the strongest disease associations.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Evidence For Targets
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced target prioritization for one disease.
prompt_templates.prompt: For Parkinson disease, compare the top associated targets by evidence type, association score, tractability, and known drug support. Highlight review priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Design A Repurposing Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow combining disease, drug, and mechanism data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a drug repurposing review for inflammatory bowel disease using Open Targets. Include known drugs, targets, mechanisms, clinical phase, and evidence caveats.

output_examples.input: Find promising Open Targets evidence for BRCA1 in breast cancer.
output_examples.output: A concise report lists matching identifiers, association strength, supporting evidence types, known clinical context, and caveats for manual literature review.

output_examples.input: Assess whether BRAF is tractable as a drug target.
output_examples.output: The response compares tractability categories, approved or clinical drug precedence, safety notes, disease associations, and interpretation limits.

output_examples.input: Identify repurposing signals for Alzheimer disease.
output_examples.output: The response summarizes known drugs, linked targets, mechanisms of action, trial phases, and questions for follow-up validation.

best_practices: Start with verified Open Targets identifiers before interpreting associations.
Compare evidence breakdowns instead of relying only on aggregate scores.
Use downloads or BigQuery for high-volume analyses across many entities.
anti_patterns: Treating Open Targets scores as direct probabilities of clinical success.
Using text-mining evidence alone for target validation decisions.
Running broad repeated API queries when bulk data access is more suitable.

faq.question: Does this skill require Open Targets authentication?
faq.answer: No. The referenced GraphQL API is public and does not require authentication.

faq.question: Can it run large systematic screens?
faq.answer: It is designed for exploratory queries. Large screens should use Open Targets downloads or BigQuery.

faq.question: What identifiers does it use?
faq.answer: It uses Ensembl gene IDs for targets, EFO IDs for diseases, and ChEMBL IDs for drugs.

faq.question: Can it prove a target will succeed clinically?
faq.answer: No. It provides evidence summaries and ranking context that require expert interpretation.

faq.question: Which evidence types can it explain?
faq.answer: It covers genetics, somatic mutation, known drugs, pathways, RNA expression, animal models, and literature signals.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
